sources.title: Introducing Toast 1
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The August 13 launch identifies Toast 1 as a standalone search model trained for deep search and co-designed with its harness and retrieval primitives. It gives no nominal total, active count, neural architecture, or named base checkpoint. Its mentions of SID-1 and Context-1 identify related research, not lineage.

sources.title: Models
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The exact toast-1 card specifies text input/output, function calling, 131K context and 4K maximum output. It gives neither total nor active parameters and identifies no underlying base model.

sources.title: Build Your Own Harness
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The guide explicitly states that Toast 1 was trained without thinking and is served without thinking, with seq_len = 131072. Its end-to-end training description names no base checkpoint or parameter count. Context pruning removes tool-result text, not model parameters.

sources.title: Chat Completions
sources.evidence: The Toast 1 example and compatibility documentation support text conversations and function tools. The exact-model reasoning section says it has no thinking channel; reasoning_content is always null and reasoning-token usage is zero.

sources.title: Terms & Conditions
sources.evidence: The API service terms grant limited, revocable access, reserve service intellectual property and restrict extraction of underlying API structure. These support a proprietary service-license classification, not an open weight license.

sources.title: Mixedbread official public Hugging Face model inventory
sources.evidence: Refetched October 27, 2026 through the public API. The inventory still contains twelve embedding, reranking and ColBERT checkpoints, with no Toast checkpoint, card or configuration. Counts for those separately identified retrieval models do not establish Toast size.

sources.title: Research
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The research index links the Toast launch and six papers about other retrieval models; the latest listed paper is May 2026. No Toast technical report, named backbone or total/active parameter table is linked. Independent searches for Toast total size, active/activated parameters, technical reports and named-base/fine-tune lineage found no original disclosure.

sources.title: toast-harness
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026, including raw README, repository tree, config.py, token_counter.py and the BrowseComp runner. The Apache-2.0 harness accepts any OpenAI-compatible model; its default alias is toast-1 and self-hosted examples use generic policy paths. No named base, total or active count is given. Token-accounting code and a separately supplied generation backend do not disclose a neural architecture.

sources.title: BrowseComp-Plus benchmark · Toast 1
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. This exact-model comparison reports NDCG@10, p50 latency and cost for Toast 1 and RRF x3; it contains no total or activated-parameter column. RRF x3 is retrieval-result fusion, not a model parameter count.

sources.title: Changelog
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The August 13 entry records Toast 1 release. Later Toast entries concern hosted tools, context management, structured output and a playground; the changelog through October 20 gives no parameter count or named-base training lineage.

sources.title: OfficeQA-Pro benchmark · Toast 1
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The exact Toast comparison reports NDCG@10, latency and cost, including default and RRF x3 configurations. It supplies neither total nor active parameters or base-model identity.

sources.title: LongSeal benchmark · Toast 1
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The exact Toast comparison reports retrieval quality against latency and cost. It has no total/activated-parameter column and no named base-model lineage.

sources.title: OfficeQA-Pro V2 benchmark · Toast 1
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Results concern answer correctness and per-rollout cost for GPT-5.6 Sol with Toast 1 as a search sub-agent. They do not disclose Toast parameters or imply that it is derived from the answering model.

sources.title: Harvey LAB Firm Knowledge benchmark · Toast 1
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The three configurations compare the same answering model with different retrieval stacks. Reported millions are consumed tokens across 33 tasks, not total or activated model parameters.

sources.title: Toast 1 API, Pricing & Playground
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The provider page identifies mixedbread/toast-1 and lists context, output limit, price and API request parameters. It gives no model-weight count, activated count or base checkpoint; request parameters are unrelated to learned parameter counts.

name.note: The official display name has a space; its API identifier is toast-1.

developer.note: The original announcement identifies Toast 1 as Mixedbread's model.

family.note: No separate model family or underlying backbone is identified in the reviewed primary material.

release_date.note: The dated announcement says it is available that day, independently corroborated by the release changelog.

open_weights.note: Documented distribution is the hosted API under proprietary service terms. No public Toast checkpoint appears in the official model inventory; the released harness is separate software, not weights.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the hosted model under Mixedbread's service license. Apache-2.0 applies to toast-harness, not to undistributed Toast 1 weights.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 searches for total parameters, nominal size, technical reports and fine-tuned/named-base lineage found no original Toast disclosure. Reopened launch, current model card, research index, changelog, public model inventory, harness and exact-model comparisons disclose no total or named checkpoint from which a nominal count can be inherited. Descriptions of specialized training and related search agents do not establish a base-model relationship.

active_parameters_b.note: Searched active/activated parameters separately on October 27 and checked current original research and all five Toast evaluation pages. No explicit Toast active count, activated-parameter table/plot or named-base convention was found. Published values measure quality, latency, cost or consumed tokens, not activated model parameters; no equality with an unknown total is inferred.

architecture.note: The sources describe a trained search agent and retrieval harness, not its neural backbone or dense/MoE structure. First-party research and public code did not identify an exact Toast 1 architecture.

context_window.note: The exact seq_len of 131072 refines the model card's rounded 131K label and replaces the catalog's 131000 approximation. This is the served sequence limit.

modalities.note: The exact-model card specifies text in and text out. Store ingestion and retrieval over media are service features and do not establish native multimodal inputs.

reasoning.note: Explicit exact-model evidence: the guide states training and serving are without thinking, and the API docs say Toast 1 has no thinking channel. This describes dedicated thinking support, not inability to reason in ordinary text.

tool_call.note: The model accepts custom function schemas and returns function calls; hosted retrieval execution is a separate API facility.

description.value: Specialized search model for knowledge-intensive questions, multi-step retrieval, and evidence synthesis
description.note: Supported directly by the model card and launch description; no unsupported benchmark superiority or architectural claim is retained.

patch.notes: Toast 1 is a hosted proprietary model; its Apache-2.0 retrieval harness is separate software. The served context is 131,072 tokens. Mixedbread says it was trained and is served without thinking. Total and active parameters, neural architecture and named base-model lineage remain undisclosed in the reviewed sources.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains explicit null total and active counts. Fresh separate size/active searches and named-lineage checks reopened the launch, model card, research index, public checkpoint inventory, harness and changelog, and checked all five exact-model evaluation pages plus the provider card. No nominal count, active-count convention or named base supports a numerical specification. The other twelve field assessments are preserved, including the verified 131072-token context and proprietary service license.
